scout.purpose: Compose performance depends on invalidated work, parameter stability, phases, and measured runtime cost rather than blanket fear of recomposition.
scout.realWorldUse: Scrolling screens, animations, large UI trees, and frequently updated state need evidence-based diagnosis and targeted fixes.
scout.outcome: Interpret stability and skipping, capture release-mode evidence, and fix broad reads, unstable models, or expensive work at the cause.

blocks.text: A stable type lets Compose know that equal-looking inputs will not change without observable notification. Primitive values and immutable models are often stable; mutable collections and types from modules without Compose inference may be treated as unstable. When a restartable composable receives equal stable parameters, the runtime may skip it. Skipping is an optimisation, never a correctness contract. Strong skipping can expand eligibility, but developers must still preserve equality, immutability, and state ownership.

blocks.caption: An immutable UI model gives the runtime and reviewers a clear change contract.

sections.title: Measure realistic builds and user paths

blocks.text: Debug builds distort performance through tooling and disabled optimisations, so profile a release-like build with realistic data and baseline profiles where appropriate. Begin with a user-visible symptom such as missed frames or delayed input. Use system traces, Compose tracing, Layout Inspector, compiler reports, or Macrobenchmark according to the question. Counts without duration can mislead: many cheap recompositions may matter less than one bitmap decode, sort, or allocation on the main thread. Record the device, build, interaction, and before/after result.

blocks.caption: An immutable UI model gives the runtime and reviewers a clear change contract.

blocks.title: Skipping is an optimisation
blocks.text: Code must remain correct whether a composable executes or is skipped.

sections.title: Fix invalidation and cost where they occur

blocks.text: Common fixes include moving heavy pure work out of composition or remembering it with correct keys, providing stable lazy keys, deferring rapidly changing reads to layout or draw, publishing immutable collections, and splitting broad state inputs into focused values. Do not annotate a mutable class as Stable merely to silence a report; that breaks the runtime contract and can leave stale UI. A stability configuration file is an explicit promise about external types and should be reviewed like code.

A production implementation should make this topic observable and testable. Start with a concrete user outcome, then cover loading or absence, failure, recreation, rapid repeated input, long content, large font scale, and alternate navigation entry where relevant. Keep state ownership visible in parameters and keep side effects behind a lifecycle-aware boundary. Use previews for representative visual states, unit tests for pure state transformation, Compose UI tests for semantics and interaction, and runtime inspection only when the question depends on scheduling, layout, drawing, or device behaviour. Document any trade-off that a future maintainer cannot infer from the code. Correctness means the feature still behaves predictably when recomposition, cancellation, configuration change, or user timing differs from the happy-path demonstration.

steps.label: Name contract
steps.detail: State the owner, lifetime, inputs, output, and cancellation behaviour.

steps.label: Implement
steps.detail: Use the narrowest API that expresses the required lifecycle and semantics.

steps.label: Exercise
steps.detail: Cover normal, empty, failure, recreation, and rapid-interaction states.

steps.label: Observe
steps.detail: Use tests, inspection, or traces appropriate to the behaviour.

steps.label: Refine
steps.detail: Change the measured cause while preserving explicit ownership.

blocks.title: Never lie with stability annotations
blocks.text: Unnotified mutable fields can prevent required recomposition and display stale state.

walkthrough: The public var can change without a snapshot notification.
The Stable annotation promises changes will be observable and equality is reliable.
Use immutable published models or snapshot-backed observable properties.
inspect.expectedOutput: Every total change follows observable state and renders correctly with or without skipping.

trap_check.mistake: Profiling only a debug build with tiny data.
trap_check.why: Tooling overhead and unrealistic inputs hide production bottlenecks.
trap_check.fix: Measure a release-like build and reproducible representative interaction.

trap_check.mistake: Optimising or abstracting before the behaviour is measured.
trap_check.why: It adds machinery while the actual ownership or runtime problem remains unknown.
trap_check.fix: Write a focused test or collect runtime evidence before changing the design.

challenge_intro.task: Create a reproducibly slow Compose feed, capture release-mode evidence, apply one stability or state-read fix, and record the before-and-after result.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The scenario and device conditions are documented. The fix targets evidence rather than a guess. Correctness tests pass before and after.

recall.prompt: What does stability help Compose decide?
recall.answer: Whether equal inputs make skipping safe.

recall.prompt: Is recomposition count alone a diagnosis?
recall.answer: No, duration and user impact matter.
To layout or drawing when composition is unnecessary.
